The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 17.05.2024.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 17.05.2024 at about 3.00 to 3.10 p.m., the petitioner being a taxi driver, after dropping the passenger and while taking passenger luggage from the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AK-9098 belongs to Blue Smart company, at SCCH-10 Terminal-02 Departure, Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-11-B-7748 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to hospital and took inpatient treatment.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
The respondent No.1 being owner and the respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the present petition.
3. In pursuance to the Petition notice, though the respondent No.1 being owner has appeared before the Court though his counsel, not filed the written statement.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
SCCH-10 4.
The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:
The respondent No.2 being insurer of offending vehicle has contended that the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable.

Further, the respondent No.2 has denied the accident, manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the alleged Gopinath B vs Puttegowda M S on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180679703/
2 accident.

sentences.text: Further contended that, the petitioner has filed the false case against the offending vehicle for wrongful gain.

The respondent No.2 has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries,
medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.
SCCH-10 5.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, on 17.05.2024 at about 3.00 to 3.10 p.m., the petitioner was driving his Taxi bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AK-9098 near Terminal-2 Departure, Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-11- B-7748 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, as a result, he sustained grievous injuries ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
6.
The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and examined MRO of Fortis hospital as PW-2 and examined the doctor as PW-3 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.24.
The respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
SCCH-10 7.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :

sentences.text: 9. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 17.05.2024.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR in crime No.0107/2024 of Devanahalli Traffic PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-11-B-7748 for the commission of offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P9 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Devanahalli Traffic PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.9, it reveals that, SCCH-10 after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Puttegowda. M.S., who is none other than the driver cum owner of the offending Car for the offences punishable under Section 279 & 338 of IPC.
10.
Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P8 produced by petitioner, it appears that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

11. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the respondent No.1/
driver of the offending Car showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the police records

,
it reveal that the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. the respondent No.1 was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and has caused the accident.
SCCH-10 12.
Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a Motor Vehicles Accident Compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

sentences.text: 13. Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-11- B-7748.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:-

The petitioner contended that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Aster CMI hospital, International Airport, Bengaluru and after first aid, he was SCCH-10 shifted to Fortis hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, wherein he took inpatient treatment and spent around Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.

sentences.text:
Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.8.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
16. In this case, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.11.

On perusal of Ex.P.10 discharge summary of Fortis International hospital Limited, Bengaluru, it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to SCCH-10 the said hospital on 17.05.2024 and discharged on 18.05.2024.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.11 Discharge summary of said hospital, it reveals that the petitioner again admitted to the said hospital on 20.05.2024 and discharged on 27.05.2024.
17.
Ex.P.15 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.1,71,251/-, Ex.P.16 are the deposit receipts and Ex.P.17 are the medical prescriptions

. During the cross-examination of PW-1, he has deposed that,
out of Rs.1,75,000/- only a sum of Rs.80,000/- was reimbursed by the Health Insurance Company.

On perusal of Sl.No.1 of Ex.P.15, it appears that out of Rs.40,412/-, the Insurance company was approved only Rs.35,395/- and the petitioner has paid the balance amount of Rs.5,017/- and as per Sl.No.2 of Ex.P.15, it appears that, out of total bill amount of Rs.2,31,214/-, the insurance company has approved only Rs.75,345/- and the petitioner has paid a sum of Rs.1,55,869/-.

Hence, it appears Gopinath B vs Puttegowda M S on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180679703/
5 that though the Health insurance company has reimbursed the SCCH-10 portion of medical bills,
the balance amount was paid by the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it appears that the petitioner after deducting the reimbursed amount has calculated the total medical bills as Rs.1,71,251/-.
The medical bills produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills and same is rounded off to Rs.1,72,000/- under the head of Medical expenses.
18. As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.
19. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury he has undergone surgery and suffering from permanent disability.
He has further stated that, due to the disability SCCH-10 he has lost his earning capacity.
In order to establish the disability, the doctor was examined before the Court as PW3.

PW-3 during his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained right knee quadriceps tendon rupture with morel lavellee lesion over he right knee and treated with right knee quadriceps tendon ruptures, debridement, blood clot evacuation.

Further deposed that, recently for assessment of disability, he examined the petitioner on 22.09.2025 and the petitioner has suffered physical disability of the right lower limb at 36% and 12% to the whole body.
Though PW-3 doctor was cross-examined by the counsel for the respondent No.2, nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to disprove his evidence.
20. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 35 years at the time of accident and he was a Taxi driver at Blue Smart Company, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In order to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Hence, the SCCH-10 notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/-.
The accident was occurred on 17.05.2024.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
21. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the SCCH-10 petitioner in his future earnings.
22. As per the doctor, the whole body disability is approximately 12%.
It is settled principles that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 12% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future Gopinath B vs Puttegowda M S on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180679703/
6 earning capacity as 10%.
23.

sentences.text: To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.12.

As per Ex.P.12,
the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 08.12.1985.
The accident was occurred on 17.05.2024.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 39 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable for his age is 15.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 10%.
The annual income is assessed SCCH-10 Rs.1,98,000/-(Rs.16,500 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,98,000/-(annual income) X 15 (multiplier) X 10% = Rs.2,97,000/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.2,97,000/-.
24.
The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.

Hence, I conclude that if Rs.50,000/-
is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.

25 . Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;
Sl.
 Heads Compensation No.
1) Medical expenses Rs. 1,72,000/-
2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/-
3) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 10,000/-
 SCCH-10  Loss of Future earning Rs. 2,97,000/-
4) capacity due to permanent  disability 5) Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
 Total Rs.5,69,000/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,69,000/-.
26. REGARDING LIABILITY:
As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.
In this case, the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the Gopinath B vs Puttegowda M S on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180679703/
7 respondent No.1.

entities.text: Gopinath B vs Puttegowda M S on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 RC owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 insurer are jointly SCCH-10 and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.5,69,000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,69,000/- (Rupees Five Lakh Sixty Nine Thousand only) with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the SCCH-10 compensation.

The respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 30% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
